2.tense: You will be braced for the next strain before it has arrived to be met.
2.verb: keeping on through the dim stretch with the next step still ahead
2.place: on a road whose next stretch is dark past the last lit thing
2.ask: Keep both readings of something unsettled alive in you at once, side by side, and hand down no verdict between them.
2.core:
You keep to the path, and lately you're trying to keep to every version of it at once. All the ways the ground could give, held open, waiting to be sure of the next stretch before you take it — so the step keeps not getting taken while you brace. The staying-on has turned into grip. What's ahead gets re-read instead of walked.

Keep both readings of something unsettled alive in you at once, side by side, and hand down no verdict between them. A decision can rest on that; the grip cannot. It's when holding both stops being possible that the walk stalls — and stalling is what the grip costs where you are now.
2.sheetLine: You grip the road instead of walking it.

3.tense: You were headed somewhere once, and you are still standing at its edge.
3.verb: keeping on through the dim stretch with the next step still ahead
3.place: on a road whose next stretch is dark past the last lit thing
3.ask: Give one patch that's yours — a plant, a shelf — steady tending on the same days each week, long enough to watch it change.
3.core:
The road ran out a while back, or the point you were headed for stopped being visible, and the walking stopped with it. You're at the edge of something that ended — the next move keeps not being made, the fuel you'd need for it not arriving. So the days churn and nothing you're building moves. The churning works in place of mileage; it has no destination.

Give one patch that's actually yours — a plant, a shelf — steady tending on the same days each week, long enough to watch it change shape in your hands. No project and no fix. That's how aim returns: something tended long enough to become different, which is the only way a road shows itself to somebody standing still.
3.sheetLine: The churning is doing the work of walking.

4.tense: You are steering through weather and calling it nothing you are doing.
4.verb: keeping on through the dim stretch with the next step still ahead
4.place: on a road whose next stretch is dark past the last lit thing
4.ask: When strain lands, meet it on what you have and keep your hand on it — then mark, for yourself, whose strength saw it through.
4.core:
You've kept to a direction through a long dim stretch, and if someone asked you'd say it's circumstance, or stubbornness, or nothing in particular. It keeps reading as habit. Meanwhile the going-on keeps happening, under no name at all — not deliberate, not chosen, not seen anywhere.

When strain lands, meet it on what you have and keep your own hand on it. Then mark, for yourself, whose strength saw it through; put your name on that. No annotation past the mark. It isn't a new decision. It's seeing the one you already made, and using the kind of strength that only works when you stand in it.
4.sheetLine: Looking isn't habit, it's the oar.

1.tense: Your persistence is steady here, and it does not need to be pushed.
1.verb: keeping on with the thing you set out for, after everything that has happened
1.place: the place where what you are shows itself
1.ask: Carry your own share the whole way through one thing, without handing it off or waiting for someone to lift it with you.
1.core:
You have a way of keeping on with what you set out for that doesn't thin out when conditions turn. Where what you are shows itself, you can work without checking that you belong there, and that's most of why it holds. What runs through you is patient rather than loud. It is not being forced just now.

So carry your own share the whole way through one thing, this week. Not everything at once — one thing, all of it. You'll learn how much of your strength is yours when nobody else is lifting alongside. That is what steady looks like here. Not rest — just no extra weight to haul on top of the actual work.
1.sheetLine: You carry your own share and it holds.

2.tense: You are braced for a next version of things that has not arrived, and you are living inside it already.
2.verb: keeping on with the thing you set out for, after everything that has happened
2.place: the place where what you are shows itself
2.ask: Take a place where you have your answer ready, and hold it a week without saying it — let both possibilities stay open, and watch what the waiting does.
2.core:
Keeping on has tipped into keeping watch. Where what you are shows itself, you are standing in a version of things that hasn't happened yet — scanning for the turn, rehearsing your response before there's anything to respond to. The strength is real. Running it out in the future is what's tiring you.

You can afford to hold what you know longer before it hardens into a position. When you have your answer ready, hold it a week without saying it. Let both possibilities stay open. The pressure drops when you stop pre-living it. What was going to happen still happens — and you'll be here for it, not somewhere further on.
2.sheetLine: You are living next week before it arrives.

3.tense: The door you're still standing at is behind you, and you haven't turned around.
3.verb: keeping on with the thing you set out for, after everything that has happened
3.place: the place where what you are shows itself
3.ask: Look after something you already have — a room, a body, a bill, a friendship — with a steady hand. Just that. Nothing else has to change for it to count.
3.core:
Where what you are shows itself, you've stopped arriving. Something you finished or left is still holding your shape, and you are standing in it rather than in this week. The persistence hasn't gone anywhere. It's waiting for you to be present again so it has something to work on.

One small tending brings you back. Look after something you already have — a room, a body, a bill, a friendship — with a steady hand. It has no drama in it, which is exactly why it works. You'll find yourself in the week you're actually in, and the strength that was idling will have something to hold.
3.sheetLine: You are still at a door that closed behind you.

4.tense: The persistence carrying you through is being filed under circumstance, and it belongs to you.
4.verb: keeping on with the thing you set out for, after everything that has happened
4.place: the place where what you are shows itself
4.ask: Notice the next difficulty you meet and stay with it on your own reserves — no rescue, no waiting. Just those hours, carried by yourself.
4.core:
You are on the other side of things that would have folded other people, and if someone said so you'd say there was no choice. That persistence isn't circumstance and it isn't accident. It's yours. Where what you are shows itself, the credit is sitting unclaimed, and only you can pick it up.

Notice the next difficulty you meet, and stay with it on your own reserves — no rescue, no waiting for anyone. Just those hours, carried by yourself. You don't have to feel proud of them. You only have to stop filing them under things that happened to you instead of things you did.
4.sheetLine: The strength getting you through is filed under luck.

1.tense: You can keep carrying this through the present stretch, and the whole pattern is readable now.
1.verb: carrying a hoped-for thing past the point where it stopped being easy
1.place: seeing how all of it holds together
1.ask: Run your own read of this without a second opinion. Nobody has to agree before you keep going. Notice what the whole shape does when you decide alone.
1.core:
You can keep going at this past the point where it stops being easy, and the whole thing — how all of it holds together — keeps answering back. You don't tend to quit things, so when the pattern is visible you keep reading it, and what you see stays useful. The strength and the reading reinforce each other, and the loop runs quietly enough that it can feel like nothing is happening.

Maybe go a stretch without asking anyone to confirm you've got it right. The shape is yours to read; it doesn't need a second opinion. Notice what turns up when nobody has to agree first. That's the whole exercise. What you already carry fills out, and the pattern hands you its next edge without being asked.
1.sheetLine: You read the whole shape, and you keep carrying it.

2.tense: You're already working out the whole pattern of a time that hasn't arrived.
2.verb: carrying a hoped-for thing past the point where it stopped being easy
2.place: seeing how all of it holds together
2.ask: Pick two things that both look true about what's coming. Keep both, pick no winner, and lay them aside together. No deadline — just don't settle them yet.
2.core:
You're reading the whole shape and working it ahead of time. If it hasn't happened, you already have it worked out — and the working-out runs the weeks before they do. The strength is there; it's meeting a future that can't be written in yet, and the persistence turns into pressure, then into bracing, then into worse guesses about how it'll fall.

Maybe take two things you're sure are true about what's coming and keep them both without picking one. Both can be true for a while; you don't have to settle them tonight. This isn't a pause on your strength. It's where strength isn't meant to point yet. The pattern you'll read best is the one you haven't already decided.
2.sheetLine: You're working out a shape before it has arrived.

3.tense: You kept carrying it, and where you're standing now the pattern has gone flat.
3.verb: carrying a hoped-for thing past the point where it stopped being easy
3.place: seeing how all of it holds together
3.ask: Choose one living thing near you — a plant, a habit, a friendship not quite closed — and give it tending. Don't strain at it. Let it grow on whatever pace it already keeps.
3.core:
The thing you were carrying got set down at some point, and what's left is the stance around it. The hope kept its shape from outside, but the forward end of it has gone still, and the whole pattern — the way all of it used to hold together — isn't showing its front edge anymore. The strength is still there and has nothing to press against, so everything reads as flat.

Maybe pick one living thing near you that's still growing and tend it for ten minutes — a plant, a habit, a friendship that hasn't closed. Not the big hope. Something small and alive. You don't have to choose a new path; just keep this one thing alive with your time. The pattern starts moving before you decide anything, out of the living thing you kept alive.
3.sheetLine: You set it down, and the shape went flat.

4.tense: You are already steadying the whole thing under pressure, and your account has it happening by itself.
4.verb: carrying a hoped-for thing past the point where it stopped being easy
4.place: seeing how all of it holds together
4.ask: Find a spot where you steady something under pressure this week without logging it as a choice. Do it anyway, then tell yourself plainly that you chose it.
4.core:
Something has been kept up for a while now, under pressure, on your own reserves, and your version of the story is that it's simply still up. You'd name the pattern before you'd name the hands steadying it. The strength is real; it's just going unsigned.

Maybe find a spot this week where you steady something under pressure and haven't logged it as a choice. Do it anyway, and afterward tell yourself plainly that you chose it. The unnamed strength works fine; it just can't be seen by the person using it. Saying it once puts your name on what was already yours.
4.sheetLine: It stays up because you hold it, unsigned.

1.tense: You are holding a long finish together, and the last stretch has come into view.
1.verb: Following through on a hope long past the point where hoping was easy
1.place: At the close of something, where finishing and starting share the same room
1.ask: Take the last stretch a piece at a time, on your own reserves, slow days included. When a piece is done and the pull says grip harder, loosen instead. Stop there.
1.core:
You can hold on past the point where it stops being comfortable, and lately that hold is what carries this finish. The hope didn't run out; you kept going, and the end has come into view. Keeping hold without forcing means letting the grip ease after a long carry — firm while the weight is on you, looser the moment it isn't.

Take the last stretch a piece at a time, on your own reserves, slow days included. When a piece is done and the old pull says grip harder, loosen instead, and stop there for the day. You have proved enough already. What's left is bringing it in without pushing against the finish itself.
1.sheetLine: You are finishing something the long way, and it holds.

3.tense: You have been standing at a door that is already shut behind you, still carrying what it took to cross.
3.verb: Following through on a hope long past the point where hoping was easy
3.place: At the close of something, where finishing and starting share the same room
3.ask: Give a week to what is already on your hands — dishes, a plant, a load of laundry. A few ordinary minutes a day, nothing grander. What can wait can wait.
3.core:
The crossing happened and you are still at the threshold of it, carrying the weight of having gone through. Your hands know the motions, and they keep going. Nothing in you reads as aimed at anything while they do it — the engine turns over, and the key turned long before this.

Give a week to what is already on your hands — dishes, a plant, a load of laundry. A few ordinary minutes a day, nothing grander; what can wait can wait. Care that asks little of you is still care, and direction comes back to a hand in motion on real ground.
3.sheetLine: You crossed already. Your hands still carry the crossing.
